referents.why: First person singular 'my' (feet) in a psalm is the psalm's own voice. No voice candidate is listed, and none of the listed candidates is the speaker, so no candidate id fits.
referents.category: first person in a psalm with no voice candidate

referents.why: Second person masculine singular 'your word' is addressed to God, whom the psalm addresses throughout. Of the candidates, only LORD (named in verse 89, a different verse) can be the one addressed.
referents.category: second person address to God in a psalm

referents.why: First person singular 'my' (path) in a psalm is the psalm's own voice. No voice candidate is listed, so no candidate id fits.
referents.category: first person in a psalm with no voice candidate

links.why: The waw of cl1 joins the second line of a couplet to the first. It is not a cause or result, so it stays a plain 'and'.

groups.why: Two lines of one Hebrew couplet answer each other. The second line has its copula and subject elided, and both lines share the subject 'word'.

none_fit.where: w3 and w10, 'my' (the psalm's own voice)
none_fit.what: The rules name a voice candidate for the psalm's first person, but the candidate list has none. Both referents are recorded as none.
